reviewType: Independent review of benchmark evidence, not a code change

A.verdictLine: A: QUALIFIED WITH LIMITS: matched-final bounded history around 9,000 rows, unequal intermediate retention, single M1/Chrome 154 17-terminal test, estimated Chrome process CPU energy; contextual losses must accompany the headline.
A.acceptableHeadline: In this 17-terminal Apple M1/headed Chrome 154 test, ghostty WebGL used about 25% less estimated Chrome process CPU energy and 31% fewer instructions than xterm WebGL for rolling logs with approximately 9,000 rows of bounded history. Final retained text matched; intermediate history size differed. Unicode/emoji and line-scroll tests used more energy and instructions, and interactive edits used about 4.85% more instructions.
limitations: The energy metric is the macOS kernel estimate of process CPU energy for the enumerated Chrome process tree, not physical GPU, display, whole-machine energy, or battery life. The GPU channel is Chrome GPU-process CPU work.

Snapshots are sequential and non-atomic. PID/type/start identities agree at both endpoints, but a process born and gone entirely between endpoints is unobservable. The Python reader and Node driver are outside allChrome.

These are descriptive paired observations on one Apple M1, headed Chrome 154.0.8037.93, 17 terminals with 40 columns and 12 visible rows, DPR 2, 120 warmup ticks and 900 paced measured ticks. They do not establish universal renderer superiority or a shipped optimization.

The bounded win is qualified for a matched-final, approximately 9,000-row history condition, not identical intermediate retained state. Linux mean retained-row exposure is +5.3533% for native, but that is not a causal proof that native CPU/energy cost is conservatively biased. No Mac trajectory was recorded.

B.verdictLine: B: QUALIFIED WITH LIMITS: prospective full-raster calibration passes; no material all-Chrome observer perturbation observed in two full-stream rolling pairs per library; not universal or statistically bounded equivalence.

settlement.acceptance: unaltered full PNG hashes, no masking or exclusions; scrollbar opacity 0 or 1 under unchanged visibility policy, then two RAFs
settlement.fairness: The bounded A driver applies the same unconditional helper to both GL and XGL. R02 acquires only xterm because original native GL calibration already passed and was preserved, not rerun.

B.interpretation: It is reasonable to treat observer perturbation as small relative to A and the large C losses for the tested full-stream rolling condition. Do not subtract an estimated overhead from any result. Calibration is not directly on bounded history, Unicode/emoji, line scroll or edits and is not an equivalence test. Other-Chrome relative increases are retained in allChrome. One elevated post-window load reading adds noise uncertainty.
limitations: R02 prospectively passes full PNG equality and repairs screenshot timing without masking or changing terminal policy. Original native calibration bytes match the prior independent review and old rejected xterm arms remain rejected. Only two full-stream rolling pairs per library were calibrated; no material aggregate perturbation was observed, not zero overhead or an equivalence bound. R02 first OFF arm ends at load 5.61; subsequent ON admission waited about 45 seconds until load 3.71.

The logical endpoint is reset plus paced writes, two RAFs, and direct target snapshots. There is no GL fence, device-completion, or physical presentation proof. Post-window text, hashing, settlement, and screenshots do not enter the measured counters.

Snapshots are sequential and non-atomic. PID/type/start identities agree at both endpoints, but a process born and gone entirely between endpoints is unobservable. The Python reader and Node driver are outside allChrome.

C.verdictLine: C: Unicode/emoji and line-scroll losses are real under this protocol; no artifact cause was found. Interactive edits loses about 4.85% in instructions; rolling Unicode logs wins under full-stream retention.

artifactAssessment.unequalInputOrWriteCount: Ruled out by independent frozen corpus/chunk reconstruction, registered framed stream hashes, observed public writes and byte counts on every target.
artifactAssessment.unequalRetainedHistoryForSmallWorkloads: Both losing workloads have 889 history rows; edits has zero. None reaches a retention cap. The bounded A trajectory cannot explain these small-history losses.
artifactAssessment.wrongRendererOrOverlayCanvas: Explicit WebGlTerminalRenderer and WebglAddon renderer; actual renderer-owned canvas identified, 560×456 backing for all targets at DPR 2.
artifactAssessment.logicalLossOrIncompleteParsing: Same visible text, full retained-text hash and row count for every target; pending parser/frame state settles; context loss false. Output style fidelity beyond the oracle is not proven.
artifactAssessment.unbalancedOrderOrWindowSelection: All four registered balanced pairs are retained, used and independently recomputed. Both order directions lose for Unicode/emoji and line scroll. No trace data or diagnostic replacements enter these baselines.
artifactAssessment.coldAtlasOrDeviceRestoration: 120-tick warmup; both losing native workloads report zero measured atlas misses/uploads and zero device restores, with 900 submitted frames per target.
artifactAssessment.wrongCounterUnitsOrNonChromeDominance: Verified reader digest and documented ABI/timebase validation, exact endpoint integer subtraction and close CDP/native CPU agreement. Renderer+GPU losses persist: Unicode energy 1.3146589/instructions 1.3433099, line-scroll energy 1.3579387/instructions 1.4141565. Higher relative otherChrome values do not cause the result.
artifactAssessment.observerOverhead: No direct calibration on these small workloads, so absolute uninstrumented equivalence is not claimed. Rolling calibration detects no material aggregate overhead but cannot conclusively rule out every workload-specific overhead hypothesis. No demonstrated artifact explains the measured losses.
artifactAssessment.screenshotTransientControls: Screenshots and hashes occur outside counter windows. Same-renderer PNG bytes agree in every C run set. The new settlement does not rescore older windows. Product widget layers remain in the measurement.

registrationAndRetention.interpretation: Available protocol, seal/stage hashes, raw order/count, unique output directories, turn ledger and custody are consistent. No evidence of a discarded valid A/C window or unrecorded replacement was found. Old failures and unrelated smoke/diagnostic completed windows remain retained and separate. This is not proof that an unlogged acquisition could not exist.

counterIdentityAndCustody.pidTypeStartAndExitIdentityChecks: Every inspected window has seven Chrome PIDs: browser, GPU, three renderers, network service and storage service; matching endpoint sets/types/start identities, zero exit identities, successful native reads and nonnegative exact integer deltas.
counterIdentityAndCustody.counterArithmetic: Python integers subtract raw before/after values, then sum disjoint per-PID channels. cpuSeconds=(ri_user_time+ri_system_time)/1e9 and energyJ=ri_energy_nj/1e9. Pair ratios use ghostty/xterm or ON/OFF as registered; report median of within-pair ratios.
counterIdentityAndCustody.counterAgreement: All reconstructed counters, channels and medians agree with recorded values at numerical precision; all raw snapshot acquisition envelopes are under 2.34 ms.
counterIdentityAndCustody.guardInterpretation: Every final admission reading is AC and load<4; higher initial readings wait before admission. Post-window gate checks AC only. B R02 first OFF load rises to 5.61 and the next arm waits; no retrospective drop is made. A and C have no recorded post-window load above 4. No thermal or continuous non-Chrome isolation proof exists.

These are descriptive paired observations on one Apple M1, headed Chrome 154.0.8037.93, 17 terminals with 40 columns and 12 visible rows, DPR 2, 120 warmup ticks and 900 paced measured ticks. They do not establish universal renderer superiority or a shipped optimization.

Final output equality covers visible text, row counts, and page-computed full retained-text digests under symmetric trimEnd normalization. Hidden-history style attributes are outside the oracle; complete retained-line arrays are not stored for an independent offline rehash.

The real renderer-owned drawing canvas has 560×456 backing attributes for every target. Xterm device-canvas dimensions agree. Mac raw snapshots do not separately store gl.drawingBufferWidth/Height. Complete widget rasters differ between products and are only required to agree within a renderer.

findings.finding: The bounded win is qualified for a matched-final, approximately 9,000-row history condition, not identical intermediate retained state. Linux mean retained-row exposure is +5.3533% for native, but that is not a causal proof that native CPU/energy cost is conservatively biased. No Mac trajectory was recorded.

R02 prospectively passes full PNG equality and repairs screenshot timing without masking or changing terminal policy. Original native calibration bytes match the prior independent review and old rejected xterm arms remain rejected. Only two full-stream rolling pairs per library were calibrated; no material aggregate perturbation was observed, not zero overhead or an equivalence bound. R02 first OFF arm ends at load 5.61; subsequent ON admission waited about 45 seconds until load 3.71.

Unicode/emoji and line-scroll energy and instruction losses are real under this instrumented protocol: every registered pair loses, with equal input, 889 history rows, final full-text hashes, real GL backings, stable identities and renderer+GPU aggregates showing the same losses. No artifact explanation was demonstrated.

Interactive edits is near parity only in estimated energy and CPU seconds; instructions are +4.8463%, failing the 1.02 guard. Rolling Unicode logs wins in the audited full-stream condition at 113,390 history rows, not an audited bounded-history Unicode result. These accompany any A headline.

Use estimated all-Chrome process CPU energy and instructions as named metrics. Lower CPU seconds alone does not overturn C losses, and neither allChrome nor the GPU-process channel is physical GPU or whole-machine energy.
